english: It was growing dark. Two warriors arrived at the pasture of the Upright One, and there his cattle were standing. The dogs were lying in sleep. Then the two, having seized the cattle, drove them away. Then it grew light. The Upright One woke up and did not see his own cattle, and his heart grew warm. He cried aloud and spoke to the two sons: "Join the swift horses to the chariot, you two! Let us follow those two men who drove our cattle." Then they climbed onto the chariot and drove the horses on. They tracked the cattle. Then at the ford they caught sight of the two. The two, trembling in fear, let the cattle go, and they were swimming through the water. The sons struck them down with javelins. Then the Upright One drove the cattle to the pasture, and men heard of his great fame. At the place of sacrifice he gave a sheep to the gods.

english: A serpent dwelt at the bottom of the sea. Then that serpent, coming forth from the sea, seized the cattle of the famous father and drove them into the water. Then the father spoke to the brothers: "Who will slay the serpent?" The brothers trembled in fear. But the Swift One stood up and said: "Father, I will slay the serpent. Give me your spear!" Then he gave it to him. The Swift One went to the sea. Then the serpent came forth out of the water. The Swift One wounded it with the spear, and he slew the serpent and split its head, and the water was red. Then the cattle came forth out of the sea, and the brothers were astonished. He gave the Swift One ten cattle and said: "May imperishable fame be yours!"

english: The swift warrior was seeking the cattle of his own father. Then he arrived at a great river. The river was full, and its water had become cold, and his horses were trembling. Then he spoke to it: "River, give me a path! I shall give you poured honey." Then he put the honey into the water. The river grew slack, and he found the ford. He led the horses through the ford. On the other side the cattle were eating. Then he drove the cattle through the ford and came to the father. He grew joyful and said: "Beloved one, I shall set a famous name upon you, and your fame will be great."

english: The Light One was swimming through the sea. He grew tired and sank in the water, and his heart was trembling. Then he cried out to the two sons of Sky: "Sons of Sky, rescue me! Death is in front of me." Then the two heard him, and they joined swift horses to the chariot. The horses carried the chariot over the sea. Then the two drew him out of the water and seated him in the chariot. Then they transported him to his father. He caught sight of him and grew joyful. He gave the two ten horses, and their fame became great.

english: The warriors were sitting around the king. They had seized cattle and a woman. Then the giver of good things spoke: "This woman shall be mine." Then the Free One stood up and said: "King, I seized her with my spear. She shall not be yours." The king said to them: "Seize this woman!" Then they took her and led her to him. Then the Free One went away to his own chariot and sat down by the sea, and his tears were flowing. There he spoke a word: "I shall not enter the fight for the giver of good things. May his warriors fall!" Then the fight was great, and they grew cold. But the Free One was sitting at the chariot and did not lift his spear.

english: A javelin wounded the Good One. The Good One fell from the chariot and lay upon the earth. His brother arrived and lifted him with his hands. The Good One spoke: "Brother, death has arrived for me. Lead my horses to the mother and say to her: 'Your son did not tremble before death.'" Then he died. The brother transported him by chariot to the mother. She caught sight of him and cried aloud, and her tears were flowing: "Beloved son, you lie upon the earth. You will not see the dawn, and you will not drive the swift horses. But your fame will not vanish." Then they laid him upon the fire, and the brother spoke to Fire: "Fire, carry my brother to the gods!" Then the fire burned him. Men remember his imperishable fame.

english: For ten years the king was going about on the sea. Then he arrived at the pasture. He was wearing wool, and he was covering his head, and the men did not know him. That dog of his was lying in the stall. The dog saw him and knew him, and it licked his hand. Then the dog grew cold. He went to the woman. Ten men were sitting there, and they were eating his cattle. The woman said to him: "Who are you?" "I am your husband. I have arrived." She said to him: "If you are my husband, tell me the name of your father." Then he spoke the famous name of his own father, and the woman knew him and grew joyful. Then he seized the spear and killed those ten men. Then he sat down with her, and his fame became good.

english: Two warriors came forth out of the troops, and the two were standing face to face, and they lifted their javelins. Then Eagle spoke: "Whose son are you?" "My name is Wolf. My father was the guest of the Long One." Then Eagle grew joyful and put his javelin into the earth: "The Long One was my father. Your father used to sit at our fire, and my father gave him two horses. You are my guest. I indeed remember the pledge. Let us two not enter the fight! Let us two give our javelins in exchange." english: The Drunken One was drinking honey, and he killed a man. He had a brother. The brother heard the word, and his heart grew warm: "I shall not eat, and I shall not drink. Let me find him!" Then the brother, grasping a javelin, followed him. The Drunken One had gone onto a high hill and was lying in sleep. The brother climbed it and saw the Drunken One lying. Then he cried aloud: "Drunken One, wake up! I am the brother of him whom you killed." Then the Drunken One woke up and stood up, and he was trembling. Then the brother bored through his heart with the javelin, and the Drunken One died. Then he drank honey and grew joyful, and his fame was imperishable.

english: The father went away. His son grew up and became a warrior, and in his youth he grew strong. Then the father arrived with a troop, and the warrior stepped against him: "Warrior, who is your father?" "My father went away. Men say: 'He vanished.'" "I am your father." "I do not trust you. Lift your spear!" Then he said: "I shall strike down my son, or my son will strike me down." Then the two struck. The father's spear bored through his heart. The warrior fell to the earth and spoke: "Now, father, I have come to know you." Then he died. He cried aloud and lay down beside him: "Your fame will be imperishable. May death seize me!"

english: The lord had ten horses in the stall. When it was growing dark, the troop came to the stall. The dogs were lying in sleep. The troop stole the horses and led them over the hill. At dawn the lord did not find them. But his dog had heard them, and it pointed out the path to him. Then the lord followed them with the brothers. By the river they caught sight of the troop. It was cooking a horse. The lord cried aloud: "You stole my horses! Now death will seize you!" Then the troop said: "Lord, do not kill us! We shall give you ten cattle." Then the lord took the cattle and the horses and drove them to the stall, and his fame became great.

english: The serpent was lying around the hill, and it had enclosed the waters. The earth dried up, and the bloom vanished, and the cattle were thirsty. The gods said to Perkʷunos: "Perkʷunos, slay the serpent! Free the waters!" Perkʷunos, drinking honey, grew strong. He went to it and struck the serpent. The serpent stood up against him. Then Perkʷunos slew the serpent and split the hill. The waters came forth out of the hill, and the rivers were going to the sea. Then it rained. The cattle drank, and the earth was productive, and bloom came forth. The gods said: "Perkʷunos, you who slew the serpent, you who freed the waters, your fame is imperishable."

The strangers arrived at the ford, and the chariots entered the water. Then they stood up and struck them with javelins. The water was red. The wheels broke, and they sank in the water. The king seized their horses and gave them to the son-in-law and said: "Son-in-law, you were awake. Good fame is yours."

english: The brother fell from the chariot, and his head became cut. He was lying on the earth, and he did not wake up. His dear one lifted him and was carrying him to his sister. The sister caught sight of her own brother and cried aloud. Then she heated water and smeared honey on his head, and she covered his head with wool. english: Strangers seized the sister of the two brothers and led her into their own stronghold. The stronghold was high, and its wall was long. The two brothers went to the wall and cried aloud: "Sister, are you alive?" The sister heard them and said: "I am alive. They are guarding me." When it was growing dark, they climbed the wall. They were lying in sleep. Then the brothers caught sight of the sister and freed her. But the lord of the stronghold woke up and followed them. At the ford the two stood up against him and killed him. Then the sister swam through the river with the brothers, and their father grew joyful, and their fame is imperishable.

english: The Hale One wanted to see the wheel of the sun. He was going along the path of the sun. For a year he was walking, and his nails split. He swam through waters and climbed hills. Then he arrived at the sea. There the sun came forth out of the water. The wheel of the sun was burning, and its light was great. The Hale One was astonished and spoke to the sun: "Sun, where is my father?" The sun said: "He is with the gods. He drank honey, and he is satisfied. Go to your mother! When you die, you will see him." The Hale One arrived at her and told her the word of the sun, and the mother's heart grew warm.
